summary: Node 14 has no reassign: good edge proposed against wrong chunk is unrecoverable
description:
`reclassify` at node 14 changes the edge *type* (PARALLELS / CONTRASTS /
surface_only / unrelated). It cannot move an endpoint. So when the proposer
aims a genuinely good pairing at the neighbouring chunk, review can only
discard it.

## Evidence (yoga-sutras node 14 pass, 696 edges)

plotinus-select-works-index.404 was proposed against yoga-sutras-book-04.016
and belongs against 04.015:

  Plotinus: "it is impossible, in fact, that the collocation of material
  entities should produce life, or mindless entities mind"
  IV.15 (title claim): "The paths of material things and of states of
  consciousness are distinct"
  IV.16 (what it was aimed at): matter does not depend on a single mind and
  is law-governed — anti-idealism, not anti-materialism.

Queued surface_only because there was nothing else to do with it.

The converse case shows the rate is not negligible: tertium-organum.153 was
proposed against BOTH 04.015 and 04.016, and only 04.016 earned it. Where the
proposer happens to fire at both neighbours, review picks the right one; where
it fires at one, it is luck whether that one is right.

## Why this matters more than it looks

Node 11 has `reassign` and the comparable yoga-sutras tag pass produced six of
them — i.e. six claims that review ADDED rather than subtracted. Node 14 has
no way to add, so its output is structurally subtraction-only and the loss is
invisible: nothing in review_actions records "this was right about the wrong
chunk".

## Options (not a recommendation, this needs design)

- a `retarget` action carrying a new source/target chunk pair, validated to
  exist and not duplicate a live edge
- or: allow review to queue a NEW staged_edge with reviewer provenance, which
  mirrors how node 11's reassign inserts a row
- either way the same two-step problem as node 11's reassign applies (see
  e9e17188) — the new row lands pending and needs a second apply

Related: 0b21d209 (this), e9e17188, and the node 14 workbook entry under
"Losing a good pairing aimed at the wrong chunk".
